title: Evaluating Technological Claims with Opinion Verbs

sections.content: You know *creo que*, *pienso que* and *considero que* + indicative vs *no creo que* and *no pienso que* + subjunctive from B1 Unit 7, the present perfect subjunctive (*haya hablado*) from B1 Unit 37 and the imperfect subjunctive after a past verb from B1 Unit 38. What C1 adds is putting them together in technology op-eds, where writers use formal opinion verbs (*considerar*, *estimar*, *creer*) to evaluate claims about automated systems. When negated, they trigger the present perfect subjunctive for a recent or completed claim (*No considero que el algoritmo haya garantizado la neutralidad*) and the imperfect subjunctive after a past main verb (*No creía que el modelo predictivo ocultara tanta opacidad*). By contrast, open factual questions (*¿Crees que la inteligencia artificial reduce los errores?*) normally stay in the indicative.

sections.title: Formal opinion clauses in op-ed prose
rows: Asserted judgement (*Considero que la opacidad debilita la confianza pública.*)
Negated evaluation of a completed claim (*No considero que el algoritmo haya eliminado el sesgo.*)
Past scepticism (*No creía que el modelo predictivo produjera ese sesgo algorítmico.*)
Open factual question (*¿Crees que la inteligencia artificial garantiza la neutralidad?*)

items.spanish: Considero que la inteligencia artificial exige criterios públicos para reducir la opacidad.
items.english: I consider that artificial intelligence requires public criteria to reduce opacity.

items.spanish: No considero que el algoritmo haya alcanzado una verdadera neutralidad en sus decisiones.
items.english: I do not consider that the algorithm has achieved genuine neutrality in its decisions.

items.spanish: Al principio nadie creía que un modelo predictivo pudiera reproducir el sesgo algorítmico.
items.english: At first nobody believed that a predictive model could reproduce algorithmic bias.

items.spanish: ¿Crees que el nuevo sistema mejora la transparencia o solo esconde la opacidad?
items.english: Do you think the new system improves transparency or only hides opacity?

sections.content: Match the tense of the subjunctive to the time of the claim. After present *no considero que*, use *haya* + participle for a completed past action (*no considero que haya resuelto*); after past *no creía que*, shift to the imperfect subjunctive (*no creía que pudiera*).
